DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Sentry User Auth Token', 'detail': 'Generate a read-only token for Holmes to call the Sentry API through the hosted MCP.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': '- Sign in to Sentry and open **Settings → Account → API → Auth Tokens**
  https://sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/
- Click **Create New Token**
- Grant these read scopes only:
  - `org:read`
  - `project:read`
  - `event:read`
- Copy the token immediately (it is shown only once) and keep it for the next step', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Store the Sentry token as a secret in the robusta namespace so the runner can read it.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic sentry-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token='<YOUR_SENTRY_USER_AUTH_TOKEN>'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge this into your existing generated_values.yaml (do not create a new file).', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: sentry-mcp-token
          key: token

  mcp_servers:
    sentry-custom:
      description: "Sentry error tracking - read issues, errors, and projects"
      icon_url: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/sentry/362D59"
      docs_url: "https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Sentry-Bearer <env.SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use
        Use this data source when the user is investigating application errors, exceptions, or crashes tracked in **Sentry**, or asks about Sentry projects.

        ## Preferred tools (read-only)
        - Use `find_organizations` / `find_projects` to list Sentry organizations and projects.
        - Use `find_issues` / `search_issues` to look up open issues and error groups, filtering by project, environment, status, or query.
        - Use `get_issue_details` (or equivalent) to read the full stack trace, breadcrumbs, tags, and latest event for a specific issue.
        - Use `find_events` / `search_events` when the user needs individual error events or wants to filter by tag, release, or timestamp.

        ## Guidance
        - This integration is **read-only**: do NOT invoke any mutating tools (create / update / resolve / assign / comment).
        - Scope queries by `organization_slug` and `project_slug` when the user names them; otherwise list projects first.
        - Cross-reference Sentry errors with Kubernetes pod logs, recent deployments, and configuration changes to find the root cause.'}, {'label': 'Apply the Helm upgrade', 'detail': 'Roll out the new configuration to the robusta release on cluster prod.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=prod', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the Sentry data source', 'detail': 'Confirm Holmes picked up the new MCP server after the upgrade completes.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and for the Holmes pod in the `robusta` namespace to restart and become **Ready**
- Open the Robusta UI **Data Sources** page and confirm **Sentry** appears as enabled
- Ask Holmes something like *"List my Sentry projects"* or *"Show recent unresolved Sentry issues in project <slug>"* and confirm it returns results
- If it shows as disabled, check the Holmes pod logs for `401` / auth errors and re-check the token scopes', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})

DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Sentry auth token', 'detail': 'Generate a User Auth Token in Sentry with read scopes.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': '- Log in to Sentry and open **Settings → Account → User Auth Tokens** (or **Settings → Auth Tokens** for an org-wide token).
- Click **Create New Token**.
- Grant these read-only scopes:
  - `org:read`
  - `project:read`
  - `event:read`
  - `issue:read`
- Copy the token value once - you will paste it into the Kubernetes secret in the next step.

Relevant docs:
https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/
https://docs.sentry.io/account/auth-tokens/', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Store the Sentry auth token as a secret in the robusta namespace so Holmes can read it.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic sentry-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token='<PASTE_YOUR_SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN>'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge this snippet into your existing generated_values.yaml under holmes.', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: sentry-mcp-token
          key: token
  mcp_servers:
    sentry-custom:
      description: "Sentry MCP server - read issues, errors, events, and list projects."
      icon_url: "https://sentry.io/_assets/logo-sentry.svg"
      docs_url: "https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Bearer <env.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use Sentry
        Use this data source whenever the user asks about **application errors, exceptions, crashes, or Sentry issues**, or wants to know **what projects exist in Sentry**.

        ## What to do
        - To answer "what projects do we have?" or scope a search, call the **list projects / organizations** tools first to discover valid `organization_slug` and `project_slug` values.
        - To investigate an error, incident, or user report, use the **list issues / search issues** tools (filter by project, environment, timeframe, or search query) and then fetch **issue details** and the **latest event / stack trace** for the specific issue.
        - Always include the exact **issue ID / short ID**, title, culprit, event count, user count, first/last seen, and a short excerpt of the stack trace or error message in your answer.

        ## Constraints
        - This is **read-only** access - do NOT resolve, ignore, assign, delete, or otherwise mutate Sentry issues, even if a mutating tool appears available.
        - Prefer narrow queries (specific project + short time window) over org-wide scans to stay within Sentry rate limits.
'}, {'label': 'Apply the Helm upgrade', 'detail': 'Redeploy Robusta so Holmes picks up the new MCP server.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=prod', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Sentry shows up as a data source and the tools work.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and the Holmes pod in the `robusta` namespace to restart and become Ready.
- Open the Robusta UI and check the **Data Sources** list - `sentry-custom` should appear as connected.
- Ask Holmes something concrete to exercise the tools, for example:
  - `List my Sentry projects`
  - `Show the most recent unresolved issues in Sentry for project <your-project-slug>`
- If a call fails with a 401/403, re-check the token scopes (`org:read`, `project:read`, `event:read`, `issue:read`) and that the `sentry-mcp-token` secret exists in the `robusta` namespace.', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})

DataSourceSetupGuide({'steps': [{'label': 'Create a Sentry User Auth Token', 'detail': 'Create a personal auth token in Sentry with read-only scopes for issues, errors, and projects.', 'kind': 'app_config', 'instructions': '- Sign in to Sentry and open **Settings → Account → User Auth Tokens**
  https://sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/
- Click **Create New Token** and give it a name like `holmes-mcp`
- Grant these read-only scopes:
  - `org:read`
  - `project:read`
  - `event:read`
  - `issue:read`
- Copy the token value once - you will need it in the next step. Sentry only shows it once.', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Create the Kubernetes secret', 'detail': 'Store the Sentry auth token in a secret the Robusta runner can read.', 'kind': 'secret', 'instructions': '', 'command': "kubectl create secret generic sentry-mcp-token -n robusta --from-literal=token='<paste-your-sentry-auth-token>'", 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Add the Helm values', 'detail': 'Merge into your existing generated_values.yaml under holmes:.', 'kind': 'helm', 'instructions': '', 'command': '', 'yaml': 'holmes:
  additionalEnvVars:
    - name: SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: sentry-mcp-token
          key: token

  mcp_servers:
    sentry-custom:
      description: "Sentry - error monitoring and issue tracking (hosted MCP at mcp.sentry.dev)"
      icon_url: "https://cdn.simpleicons.org/sentry/362D59"
      docs_url: "https://docs.sentry.io/product/sentry-mcp/"
      config:
        url: "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp"
        mode: streamable-http
        headers:
          Authorization: "Sentry-Bearer <env.SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN>"
      llm_instructions: |
        ## When to use
        Use Sentry to investigate application errors and exceptions reported by services, and to answer questions about Sentry projects, issues, and events.

        ## What to do
        - **List projects** in the org when the user asks what is in Sentry, or to scope a query - use the `find_projects` / project listing tools.
        - **Find and read issues** (grouped errors) - use `find_issues` / `get_issue_details` to fetch title, status, culprit, first/last seen, event counts, and stack trace.
        - **Read specific events** (individual error occurrences) with `get_event_details` when you need the full stack trace or event payload.
        - When correlating with a Kubernetes incident, filter by service/project name, environment, release, and time window that match the alert.

        ## Constraints
        - **Read-only** - the configured token only has read scopes (`org:read`, `project:read`, `event:read`, `issue:read`). Do NOT call any tool that creates, updates, resolves, assigns, or deletes issues, comments, or projects.
        - Prefer the smallest scope: pick the right `organization_slug` / `project_slug` before broad queries.
'}, {'label': 'Apply the Helm upgrade', 'detail': 'Roll out the new Robusta values so Holmes picks up the Sentry MCP server.', 'kind': 'deploy', 'instructions': '', 'command': 'helm upgrade robusta robusta/robusta --values=generated_values.yaml --set clusterName=prod', 'yaml': ''}, {'label': 'Verify the connection', 'detail': 'Confirm Holmes picked up Sentry and can call it.', 'kind': 'verify', 'instructions': '- Wait for the Helm upgrade to finish and for the Holmes pod in the `robusta` namespace to restart.
- Open the **Data Sources** page in Robusta and confirm **Sentry** appears as an enabled data source.
- Ask Holmes something that exercises it, for example:
  - `List my Sentry projects`
  - `Show recent unresolved issues in Sentry for project <your-project-slug>`
- If it shows as disabled, check the Holmes pod logs for a `401 Unauthorized` from `mcp.sentry.dev` - that indicates the token is missing scopes or the secret was not created correctly.', 'command': '', 'yaml': ''}]})
